prompt_text: I need a dental implant in Chicago. Which specific dental practices should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Chicago for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: start by calling an academic/medical center oral surgery or periodontics department plus a couple of high-volume private implant practices. Those three types give you access to advanced imaging, multidisciplinary treatment (surgeon + prosthodontist), and lots of experience with complicated cases.

Because I don’t have live directory access, I can’t pull current phone numbers. Below are recommended specific places (types and institutions that serve Chicago) and why to call them — and a quick checklist of what to ask when you call. If you tell me your Chicago zip code and any insurance or budget constraints, I can get more targeted recommendations or suggest specific private practices near you.

Places to call (and why)

1) University of Illinois at Chicago (UIC) — College of Dentistry, Department of Periodontics / Implant Clinic
- Why: academic oversight, faculty specialists and residents, multidisciplinary review boards, often handle complex cases. Good if you want evidence-based care, comprehensive evaluation, or potential cost savings through a teaching clinic (with supervised residents).

2) Northwestern Medicine / Northwestern Memorial Hospital — Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery (OMS) or dental service line
- Why: hospital-based oral surgeons who handle complex extractions, bone grafting, sinus lifts, medical comorbidities, IV sedation, and hospital privileges if needed. Good if you have medical issues or need advanced surgery.

3) Rush University Medical Center — Division of Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery / Prosthodontics
- Why: another major academic center with coordinated care between oral surgeons and prosthodontists; good for full-arch restorations and medically complex patients.

4) High-volume private implant practices (search with AAID / AAOMS / AAP directories)
- Why: many experienced private specialists focus on implants, offer digital planning/CBCT, guided surgery, and streamlined restoration with in-house labs or trusted prosthodontists. If you want faster scheduling or concierge-style service, call a few well-reviewed private implant specialists near you.

5) Prosthodontist or multidisciplinary implant center
- Why: for the final crown, bridge, or full-arch prosthesis, a prosthodontist (specialist in restoring teeth) is important. Look for centers that pair the surgeon and a prosthodontist so the implant is planned with the final tooth in mind.

How to find reputable Chicago providers now
- Use professional directories:
  - American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons (AAOMS) “find a surgeon”
  - American Academy of Implant Dentistry (AAID) “find a dentist”
  - American College of Prosthodontists directory
  - Illinois State Dental Society / Chicago Dental Society referrals
- Check Google Maps and Yelp for patient reviews, but prioritize clinical credentials (board certification, specialty).

What to ask when you call (quick checklist)
- Are you an oral surgeon, periodontist, or prosthodontist? Board certifications?
- How many implant cases do you place per year? Experience with my specific case (single tooth, multiple, full-arch)?
- Do you do CBCT (3D) imaging in-office and guided implant planning?
- Who will place the implant and who will restore the crown/bridge/prosthesis? (same office or coordinated prosthodontist?)
- Do you perform bone grafts or sinus lifts if needed?
- Sedation options (local, oral, IV)?
- Estimated timeline from extraction → implant → restoration, and typical costs or range (and what’s included: implant fixture, abutment, crown, imaging, bone graft).
- Warranty/guarantee and follow-up schedule.
- Do you accept my insurance, or offer financing?

Next step
- Tell me your Chicago zip code, whether you have dental insurance, and whether you prefer an academic center vs private practice, and I’ll list specific private practices near you (names, addresses, and contact suggestions) and help you prioritize which to call first.
